root_cause.text: In the mm subsystem, `do_swap_page()` immediately retries and spins when `folio_trylock()` fails on a device-private folio instead of waiting for the folio to be unlocked, which can starve CPU-bound work items (such as those from `lru_add_drain_all()`) required by the lock holder to release the folio.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "If hmm_range_fault() fails a folio_trylock() in do_swap_page, trying to acquire the lock of a device-private folio for migration, to ram, the function will spin until it succeeds grabbing the lock," which can starve a work item scheduled on the same CPU. The patch resolves this in `mm/memory.c` by replacing `pte_unmap_unlock(vmf->pte, vmf->ptl)` with `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, vmf->ptl)` to wait for the locked folio to be released.

The group adds a fallback stub for a function (likely migration_entry_wait_on_locked or similar, referred to as softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked) which is used to wait on a locked folio instead of spinning, directly addressing the build requirements for the fix of the described vulnerability.
The group only updates kernel-doc documentation and does not modify any functional code related to the spinning/retry behavior in do_swap_page().
The group only adds a comment clarifying page table lock requirements, which is a documentation change and does not address the functional spinning/starvation issue described in the root cause.

The group addresses page fault synchronization and migration wait helpers, specifically fixing issues where the system needs to wait on a locked entry (such as a device-private/migration entry) during a page fault, which directly relates to the root cause of spinning instead of waiting for a locked folio to be released.
